Sometimes I ask myself where the turning point in my life had been.

That evening, we were huddled together, just as we were every day, doing our best to endure the cold and the darkness.

A violent, abusive drunk.

My head was being held down against the floor.

Christmas.
At the time, I only knew that Christmas was supposed to be a day where families share warmth and love.
Come to think of it... that was indeed Christmas Day.
Shrieking and roaring melted into one.
The walls were shaking, but not from the battering of anything as forgiving as the wind.
Kannu had grabbed Mom's face and smashed it against the window.

Violence, again and again.

That was the moment all emotion within me died.

That snow would go on to emotionlessly cover everything, and for once, I understood its mercy.

Kyousuke: “I'm sorry, Dad...”
That was the moment I was reborn.
My heart was already frozen to the core. I had no feelings whatsoever.

God, please save me.

A body immune to the elements, standing like a monster from the peaks of the snowiest mountain.

To say such things at this point...

I should go to bed now.

As long as it's for the sake of money, there's no information I won't hesitate to dig up. And the ends always justify the means, no matter how dirty they may be.

Hearing someone use his full name, my typically light-hearted liaison used a thick, deep voice to respond in a serious manner. ‘Of course, I'll take care of it.’
To ensure adequate preparation, I gave detailed instructions to Mikimoto.
Winter nights are long, their darknesses deep, and they quickly seep into an unsteady heart.
